# CloudEval CLI

CloudEval CLI is an agent-ready command line interface for CloudEval cloud
evaluation workflows. It supports interactive terminal chat, non-interactive
one-shot questions, non-interactive agent tasks, project creation from cloud
templates, cost and Well-Architected Framework reports, billing commands, and a
stdio MCP server for agents.

## Install

```bash
curl -fsSL https://cli.cloudeval.ai/install.sh | bash
cloudeval login
```

## Agent-Safe Commands

Use JSON output for automation:

```bash
cloudeval capabilities --format json
cloudeval help agents
cloudeval status --format json
cloudeval doctor --format json
cloudeval models list --format json
cloudeval projects list --format json
cloudeval reports list --format json
cloudeval credits --format json
cloudeval billing summary --format json
```

Use `ask` for direct one-shot answers:

```bash
cloudeval ask Summarize this project --project <project-id> --format json --non-interactive
```

Use `agent` for deeper agent-mode execution:

```bash
cloudeval agent Find cost and architecture risks --project <project-id> --format json --non-interactive
```

Quotes are optional for simple multi-word prompts because the CLI joins
remaining words. Use quotes when a prompt contains shell metacharacters, leading
dashes, newlines, or spacing that must be preserved.

For text, JSON, and markdown output, ask/agent progress events are written to
stderr. Use `--progress none` or `--quiet` to suppress progress. Use
`--format ndjson --progress ndjson` when an agent needs progress and answer
events on stdout. If the backend completes without final answer content, the
command exits non-zero with a clear no-final-response error.

## Default Mode

The terminal UI supports Ask and Agent modes. Set the active profile default:

```bash
cloudeval setup --mode agent --non-interactive
cloudeval config set mode agent
cloudeval config get mode --format json
```

After saving a default mode, `cloudeval`, `cloudeval tui`, and `cloudeval chat`
start with that mode selected.

## MCP

Start a local stdio MCP server:

```bash
cloudeval login
cloudeval mcp serve --toolset readonly
```

MCP tools include `capabilities_get`, `projects_list`, `projects_get`,
`projects_export_diagram`, `ask`, `reports_list`, `reports_run`,
`reports_download`, `billing_summary`, `billing_usage`, `billing_ledger`, and
`open_url`.

## Privacy

The CLI redacts account IDs, session IDs, tenant IDs, checkout session IDs, and
sensitive URL query parameters by default. Use `--show-sensitive-ids` only in a
trusted local workflow. Do not paste tokens, session databases, smoke artifacts,
project report JSON, customer emails, billing ledger data, or local
`~/.config/cloudeval` contents into public issues or prompts.
